papers.title: Leakage-Suppressed Encrypted Keyword Queries over Multiple Cloud Servers
papers.abstract: Searchable encryption is a technique that can support operations on encrypted data directly. However, searchable encryption is still vulnerable to attacks that exploit the leakages from encrypted query results. This article presents an effective multi-server searchable encryption scheme to prevent volume and access pattern leakages. The proposed scheme distributes the encrypted data across multiple servers and uses a novel query processing algorithm that prevents any single server from learning the full query pattern. We provide a formal security analysis to prove the security of the scheme against various adversarial models. We also implement a prototype and evaluate its performance using real-world datasets. The experimental results show that the scheme achieves strong security guarantees with acceptable overhead, making it practical for deployment in cloud environments.
